what: C14: why the partitioned scan's peak grew with the corpus at a fixed partition size, and what the fix changed
host: Windows Server 2019, 6 CPUs, Python 3.14, SQLite (the bounded runs)
method: scratch diagnostics around backend.partitioned_scan.run_partitioned_scan: tracemalloc per phase (plan, each partition, finalize), gc referrer tracing, the process working set sampled every 50 ms per phase; corpora written by scripts/c14_scale_harness.write_corpus

before_fix.cause: each partition's engine left its records, findings, previews and worker futures in reference cycles; no engine or future was reachable after gc.collect(), so the growth was uncollected cyclic garbage that full collections - rarer as the heap grows - left behind

fix: backend/partitioned_scan._run_unit runs gc.collect() after every partition (tests/test_c14_scale_harness.py::APartitionIsReleasedWhenItIsWrittenTest; the mutation removing it is caught)

finalize_heap_at_its_peak_mib.held_by: one partition's decoded records (store.iter_partition_records) - the design: one partition in memory at a time

after_fix.residual: the live Python heap is flat; the remaining working-set growth is memory the allocators keep after it is freed (not attributed further on this host). A linear projection of it is not a claim: whether it plateaus is what the 200,000-file run on a scale host measures, at DSPM_PARTITION_MAX_FILES 2000 and 500.

gate_status: HELD FOR SCALE HOST - partitioning stays off by default (DSPM_PARTITIONED_SCANS=0) until the 200,000-file run passes
